advice_uk_to_pt.detail: Public update 12 November 2026: 'Removal of information on severe weather'. The record shows 'New information about severe weather' on 10 November 2026 and 'Updated information on European Entry-Exit System (EES)' on 11 August 2026. No alert status is listed on the page data (alert_status is empty).

Portugal follows Schengen rules. The passport must have a date of issue less than 10 years before arrival and an expiry date at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area. Passports renewed before 1 October 2018 may have an issue date more than 10 years ago, making them invalid for entry.

British citizens travelling on a full British citizen passport can visit the Schengen area, including Portugal, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period for tourism, family visits, business meetings, cultural or sports events, or short-term study or training. Overstaying can lead to a ban of up to 3 years. Border control may ask for an onward or return ticket and proof of enough money.

Advice says EES 'is now being implemented across the Schengen area'. On a short-stay entry you may need to register fingerprints and a photo at a booth; no cost; children aged 11 or under are not fingerprinted but can be photographed. Extra time is advised at entry and on departure by plane. The digital record is valid for 3 years. If you enter via Dover, Eurotunnel at Folkestone or Eurostar at St Pancras, details are taken before you leave the UK. The page does not give a start date in the text read.
The entry requirements text read did not mention ETIAS, so no ETIAS status or date is recorded from this source.

Children aged 17 and under travelling to Portugal alone, or with someone who is not their parent or legal guardian, must carry a letter of authorisation, signed and dated by the parent or guardian, with the signature certified by a notary or solicitor and legalised, plus a copy of the parent's passport.

You cannot take meat, milk or products containing them into EU countries, with exceptions such as powdered baby milk, baby food and special foods or pet feed required for medical reasons. Declare anything prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

Terrorist attacks in Portugal cannot be ruled out. Demonstrations are not uncommon, particularly in cities, and are mostly peaceful. Strike action that disrupts travel, including at airports, can take place and can be announced at short notice.
The advice also covers Madeira, Porto Santo and the Azores.

advice_pt_to_uk.detail: An ETA costs £20 to apply online or through the UK ETA app; no refund after applying. It lets you travel to the UK, Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man for up to 6 months for tourism, visiting family or friends, business trips or short-term study. It does not guarantee entry. The page warns that other websites may charge more.

advice_pt_to_uk.detail: 'You usually need an ETA rather than a visa if you're from Europe, the USA, Australia, Canada or certain other countries.' Each person needs one, including babies and children. Not needed by British or Irish citizens, people with UK visas or permission to live, work or study in the UK, or those transiting airside. Dual British or Irish citizens cannot get one.

gaps.what: INE guests and overnight stays by country of residence (United Kingdom), Portugal and Algarve, last 12 months, and UK rank or share
gaps.why: The INE JSON API was reachable but I could not find the indicator code for the country-of-residence breakdown. Codes 0012088, 0012089, 0012091, 0012092 and 0012093 are by segment or type only (no country). Scans of nearby codes found nothing, and several calls were reset by the proxy. Nothing was filled from memory.
